stemMd: How much heat is needed to raise 0.50 kg of water by 8 °C? Use c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹ and ignore losses.
explanationMd: Use Q = mcΔT. The calculation is 0.50 × 4200 × 8 = 16,800 J. A temperature difference of eight degrees has the same numerical size in kelvins, so no offset conversion is needed.

distractorRationale.b: This includes mass and specific heat but ignores the temperature change.
distractorRationale.a: This assumes one kilogram instead of half a kilogram.
distractorRationale.e: This divides by the temperature rise rather than multiplying.
distractorRationale.c: This is ten times too small.
